name: UVic six-course test v1
notes: Authored after development implementation; frozen before first run. Same narrow corpus and related topics limit independence. Do not tune retrieval or prompts using these results.

questions.question: Does CSC110 introduce software testing?
questions.reference_answer: Yes; the description includes an introduction to testing.

questions.question: Are objects and classes part of CSC-110?
questions.reference_answer: Yes; both are included in the description.

questions.question: Which control-flow concepts appear in CSC 110?
questions.reference_answer: Selection and iteration.

questions.question: Is CSC 110 credit compatible with CSC 111?
questions.reference_answer: Credit is granted for only one of those courses.

questions.question: Does CSC110 require every listed high-school mathematics option?
questions.reference_answer: No; the source uses alternative groups, including a university mathematics alternative. Preserve its one-of nesting.

questions.question: Is MATH120 an option in the CSC110 prerequisites?
questions.reference_answer: Yes; MATH120 appears among the university mathematics alternatives.

questions.question: Does csc115 include recursion?
questions.reference_answer: Yes; recursion is in the description. Flag the editorial instruction in the source.

questions.question: What object-oriented concepts are mentioned for CSC115?
questions.reference_answer: Abstraction, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and generic programming appear in the description; flag the editorial source wording.

questions.question: Is CSC 116 accepted instead of CSC 110 before CSC115?
questions.reference_answer: The CSC115 prerequisite alternatives are CSC110 or CSC111, not CSC116.

questions.question: Can CSC115 and CSC160 both count for credit?
questions.reference_answer: No; only one of CSC115, CSC116 and CSC160 can receive credit.

questions.question: Does taking CSC111 meet the listed prerequisite alternative for CSC115?
questions.reference_answer: Yes; CSC111 is one of the two alternatives.

questions.question: Is graph traversal discussed in CSC225?
questions.reference_answer: Yes; graph traversals, topological sorting and connectivity testing are included.

questions.question: What does CSC225 say about time and space complexity?
questions.reference_answer: Both concepts are part of the course description, along with worst-case analysis.

questions.question: Does CSC225 include self-balancing search trees?
questions.reference_answer: Yes; tree-based structures include self-balancing binary search trees and heaps.

questions.question: Can MATH122 alone satisfy all of the prerequisites for CSC225?
questions.reference_answer: No; a programming alternative CSC115/CSC116 is also required, alongside ECE242/MATH122.

questions.question: Is the pair CSC116 and ECE242 one way to satisfy the published prerequisite groups for CSC225?
questions.reference_answer: Yes, those meet the two respective one-of groups; do not guarantee registration eligibility.

questions.question: Does CSC226 introduce NP-completeness?
questions.reference_answer: Yes; it introduces P, NP and NP-completeness.

questions.question: Are network flow problems part of CSC226?
questions.reference_answer: Yes; optimization includes maximum flow problems on networks.

questions.question: What is CSC226 called in the calendar?
questions.reference_answer: Algorithms and Data Structures II.

questions.question: Can GEOG226 be taken alongside CSC226 as the listed statistics-related alternative?
questions.reference_answer: GEOG226 is explicitly a pre- or corequisite alternative; retain that official listing even if the subject seems unexpected.

questions.question: Is PSYC300A one of the concurrent-enrollment options for CSC226?
questions.reference_answer: Yes; it is one of five pre- or corequisite alternatives.

questions.question: Must I complete all five pre- or corequisite options for CSC226?
questions.reference_answer: No; the source requires one of GEOG226, PSYC300A, STAT254, STAT255 or STAT260.

questions.question: Was CSC226 formerly numbered CSC326?
questions.reference_answer: Yes; the former-course note identifies CSC326.

questions.question: Does CSC320 cover Turing machines?
questions.reference_answer: Yes; Turing machines are a typical topic.

questions.question: Are context free languages included in CSC320?
questions.reference_answer: Yes; context free languages appear among typical topics.

questions.question: Can CSC120 replace CSC226 as the prerequisite for CSC320?
questions.reference_answer: No; CSC226 is required plus one of CSC120 or ENGR130.

questions.question: Is ENGR130 allowed instead of CSC120 in the CSC320 prerequisite groups?
questions.reference_answer: Yes; either is accepted in that group, in addition to CSC226.

questions.question: Does CSC360 discuss deadlocks and CPU scheduling?
questions.reference_answer: Yes; both topics appear in its description.

questions.question: Which memory and storage topics are listed for CSC360?
questions.reference_answer: Memory management and file systems are included.

questions.question: Can ECE255 fill the architecture prerequisite alternative for CSC360?
questions.reference_answer: Yes; CSC230 or ECE255 fills that group; the other groups are still required.

questions.question: How do the descriptions of CSC225 and CSC226 differ?
questions.reference_answer: CSC225 establishes fundamental algorithms, data structures and analysis; CSC226 covers intermediate design, dynamic programming, greedy methods, network flows and NP-completeness.

questions.question: Compare the formal-theory topics of CSC320 with the systems topics of CSC360.
questions.reference_answer: CSC320 concerns formal models, languages and computability; CSC360 concerns operating system structures, concurrency, scheduling, memory and file systems.
